fields.description: Palm Jebel Ali is Nakheel’s multi-phase island destination with distinct residential fronds and villa collections. Beach and Coral homes form part of a much larger master plan. This page describes the destination and verified villa examples; it does not combine every release into one current price, payment schedule or completion date.

research.community: Palm Jebel Ali · multiple fronds and releases
overview: Nakheel’s August 2026 announcement identifies a limited 44-villa release on Frond F: Beach homes have five or six bedrooms, while Coral homes have six or seven. The advertised approximate areas for that release are not substituted for earlier design-specific plan measurements.

The reviewed earlier Beach Villas pack includes Blue Horizon, a six-bedroom G+2 example with family room and roof lounge. Its disclaimer states that illustrated landscaping and pool layouts are not provided by the developer. Buyers need the exact frond, design code and current specification.
research.locationNote: Palm Jebel Ali, Dubai, is the source-supported destination. It has no exact entry in the local taxonomy yet; areaId remains null. It must not be mapped to Palm Jumeirah or an assumed nearby mainland district.
research.priceNote: No single current destination-wide starting price was established. An earlier branded sheet advertises AED 18.1 million alongside November 2028 completion. That is a historical release reference, not a current Frond F price or a universal Palm Jebel Ali offer; the headline price is therefore left on request.
research.paymentNote: The earlier sheet has a valid 80/ 20 schedule: 20% booking, 60% dated instalments and 20% at November 2028 handover. It does not identify every applicable frond. No common payment plan is assigned to the whole destination, and no current Frond F schedule is invented.
research.handoverNote: Nakheel’s 20 August 2026 release says first villa handovers are scheduled to start in late 2026 and continue through 2027. The earlier commercial sheet estimates November 2028 for its release. These describe different delivery scopes, so there is no single destination handover headline.
